newsitem.title: USA: Broin lawyer says tobacco has edge in jury process.
newsitem.headline: Broin lawyer says tobacco has edge in jury process.

text.p: A lawyer pressing a landmark class-action suit against cigarette makers on Friday said tobacco company attorneys were ahead in the competition to seat favorable jurors after four weeks of initial screening.
"We have not been nearly as successful," Stanley Rosenblatt, a lawyer for the plaintiffs, said in court.
Rosenblatt made the remark while opposing the selection of a social worker for the pool of standby jurors to hear testimony in the case, known as Norma Broin vs. Philip Morris Cos Inc et al.

The lawyer argued the woman being screened was disposed against his suit, filed on behalf of thousands of non-smoking flight attendants whose tobacco-related illnesses were allegedly caused by breathing secondhand smoke aboard U.S passenger flights.

Rosenblatt said the lawyers opposing him -- numbering a dozen or more for Philip Morris and eight other defendants -- were highly skilled at interrogating potential jurors, and they were generally succeeding in excluding people likely favorable to his case while including others likely to agree with the tobacco companies.
Each side in the case has the right to exclude without
explanation as many as 53 people from the pool before a jury of six and 10 alternates is chosen and testimony begins.
Two people passed initial screening on Friday, bringing
the pool of standbys to 108. Kaye has said he wants a pool of 125 before a final selection is made.
Court officials said jury selection would continue into
July, and that testimony was likely to begin on July 14. A trial will likely last eight weeks or longer.
